guidelines.whenToUse:
Breadcrumbs show where the current page sits in the hierarchy and give one-click
passage back up the trail. The component renders the WAI-ARIA pattern: a labelled
`nav` landmark wrapping an ordered list, with the last item marked as the current page
and separators hidden from assistive tech.
Items with `href` render as real links. For SPA routing, omit `href` and handle
`itemClicked` — items render as link-styled buttons instead. Typography, link and
current-page colors, the separator symbol, and spacing all resolve from the theme's
`breadcrumb` options.
accessibility: Renders the WAI-ARIA pattern: a labelled `nav` landmark wrapping an ordered list.
The last item is `aria-current="page"` and not a link.
Separators are `aria-hidden` — screen readers hear the trail, not the chevrons.
Set `ariaLabel` when a page has more than one breadcrumb nav.

guidelines.whenToUse:
Navigation drawer with two modes sharing one content slot:
- **`side`** renders an in-flow `<aside>` that pushes page content — the classic
  dashboard sidenav. Opening and closing animates its width; a divider border primitive
  separates it from the content, and it is hidden from assistive tech while closed.
- **`over`** renders a native `<dialog>` in the top layer: focus trapping, Escape, and
  the scrim backdrop come from the platform, and the panel slides in from its edge
  (`position`: `start` or `end`).
`[(open)]` is two-way; Escape and backdrop clicks keep it in sync. Surface, width,
divider, elevation, padding and backdrop all resolve from the theme's `drawer` options.
accessibility: Overlay mode is a native `<dialog>`: focus is trapped by `showModal()`, Escape closes, and the backdrop click closes — all kept in sync with `[(open)]`.
Give the overlay an accessible name via `ariaLabel` (defaults to "Navigation").
A closed side drawer is `aria-hidden`, so its links leave the accessibility tree.

api.description: Explicit square size. Bare numbers are px; strings pass through, so any CSS length works (`'1.25rem'`, `'1em'`, `'clamp(…)'`). Leave it unset to keep the default behaviour — the icon fills its container, which is what lets a themed control size its own glyph through padding. guidelines.whenToUse:
Icons are adaptive svg images. By default they grow to the space allotted to them and
use the current color of the parent element — so a themed control can size its own glyph
through padding, and recoloring the container recolors the icon.
Both defaults can be overridden:
- `color` statically sets the icon color, ignoring `currentColor`.
- `size` sets an explicit square size, for call sites that would otherwise need a
  width/height CSS rule just to size one icon. Bare numbers are px; strings pass
  through, so any CSS length works.
```html
```
Leave `size` off wherever the container already defines the box — that is still the
preferred form, and it is what keeps a themed `icon-button` in control of its glyph.
accessibility: Icons are decorative (`aria-hidden`) — the parent control carries the accessible name.
Icons come from the theme's `icons` map (masked with `currentColor`); unknown names render nothing.

only after the user has interacted (touched or dirty), and `required` syncs from
`required()` validators automatically.
Project adornments with the `pre-input` / `post-input` slots. For multi-line text
use Textarea; for search semantics use Search Input.
accessibility: `label` is required and becomes the accessible name (`aria-label`).
`aria-invalid` reflects the error state once the field was touched or is dirty.
`aria-required` mirrors the `required` state synced from validators.
Link external error text with `ariaDescribedBy`.

guidelines.whenToUse:
Loading placeholder that sketches the shape of incoming content: `text` renders one or
more lines (ending on a short line, as real copy would), `rect` stands in for media and
charts, `circle` for avatars. Skeletons paint with the theme's surface tokens so they
sit naturally on any brand in both modes, and the shimmer sweep only animates for users
who allow motion — under `prefers-reduced-motion` it degrades to calm static blocks.
Skeletons are `aria-hidden`; announce loading on the container (e.g. `aria-busy`)
where your app knows what is actually loading.

for sortable columns, but can wrap any header content bound to a `UniDatasource`.

guidelines.whenToUse:
The KPI tile a dashboard leads with: a muted label, a large headline value (numbers
auto-compact — `48234` renders "48.2K"), an optional signed delta, and an optional
decorative sparkline.
The delta's color is decided by **direction × whether up is good**, never direction
alone — set `upIsGood` to `false` for measures like churn, errors, or cost, and a
falling number correctly reads as good news. The arrow is accompanied by
screen-reader text ("up"/"down"), so state never relies on color alone, and `caption`
names the comparison period.
Frame (surface, border primitive, radius), typography (the type scale's `stat` role
for values), delta inks (the semantic `success`/`error`), and sparkline colors all
resolve from the theme's `stat` options.
donts: Rely on delta color alone — the arrow + wording carry direction for everyone
accessibility: The delta arrow is decorative; screen readers hear "up"/"down" in words instead.
The sparkline is `aria-hidden` — the value and delta carry the information.

guidelines.whenToUse:
The typography primitive, applied as an **attribute on any element** so your HTML
semantics stay intact. The attribute value is the typeface —
`<h1 uni-text="display-small">` — and `[uni-text]="role()"` binds it dynamically.
With no value, the typeface is inferred from the host element (`h1` →
`headline-large`, `p` → `body-1-long`, `small` → `caption`, `blockquote` → `quote`,
falling back to `title-small`), so plain semantic markup is correctly set with zero
configuration. `color` takes any theme color token; `align`, `nowrap`, `maxWidth`,
and `ellipsis` handle common text layout.
dos: Reach for semantic elements first and let the element-aware defaults set the type
donts: Use `span uni-text="headline-large"` where a real heading belongs
accessibility: Text never replaces your elements — headings stay `h1`–`h6`, paragraphs stay `p`,
Type is styling only: pick the element for meaning, the typeface for appearance

Live preview
Pick a theme above — every registered theme (UNI_THEMES) restyles this card and these buttons instantly.

guidelines.whenToUse:
Drop-in switcher for every theme registered via `UNI_THEMES`. Renders a `uni-select` over
`ThemeService.themeOptions` and applies the choice through `ThemeService.selectTheme`, so the
selection persists across reloads exactly like any other theme change. Use it wherever an app
offers a theme choice — a settings page, an app-bar action, or a light/dark toggle backed by two
registered themes. Because it reads the registry from the injected `UNI_THEMES` token, adding a
new theme to the registry is all it takes for the switcher to offer it.
dos: Register every selectable theme in `UNI_THEMES`; the switcher derives its options from the registry.
Give the control a meaningful `ariaLabel` when "Theme" is ambiguous in context (e.g. "Editor color theme").
Use `themeChanged` for side effects like analytics or syncing a user preference to a backend.
donts: Don't call `ThemeService.theme.set()` alongside the switcher — bypassing `selectTheme` skips persistence and leaves the select out of sync.
Don't hardcode theme ids in app logic; read `ThemeService.selectedThemeKey()` instead.
Don't use it for the palette-generation workflow — that's the Theme Builder; the switcher only picks among registered themes.
accessibility: Built on a native `<select>` (via `uni-select`), so keyboard and screen-reader interaction come from the platform.
Exposes `ariaLabel` (default "Theme") as the accessible name for the control.
Theme changes restyle in place without moving focus or reloading, so context is preserved for assistive tech.

guidelines.whenToUse:
A switch-style control for turning an option on or off with immediate effect —
prefer it over a checkbox when the change applies instantly (settings, feature
switches) rather than as part of a submitted form. It implements
`FormCheckboxControl`, so it binds with the Signal Forms `[field]` directive or a
direct `[(checked)]` model.
Track, knob, and size resolve from the `toggle` theme options; the checked state
wears the active `variant` color.
dos: Use for instant on/off effects (settings, feature switches)
donts: Use in submitted forms where nothing happens until save — that is a checkbox
accessibility: Semantic `<input type="checkbox">` with `role="switch"`, properly associated with its label.
Space toggles; focus indicators are provided for keyboard navigation.
Screen readers announce the label and on/off state.
